title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
The failure here is a fabricated interface rather than a faulty model. The trading app the couple used was real, and police confirmed as much, but the website the scammer generated with AI showed investment gains that did not exist. The couple's only view of their own money was a screen controlled by the person taking it, so the false performance figures were not an error inside a working system, they were the system the victim was shown.

That places the failure at the point of verification. Small withdrawals were permitted early, which gave the couple a real result to trust, and the false gains then scaled up behind that trust. Nothing visible from inside the account could have exposed the deception, because the deception was the account view. Catching it would have required confirming the platform through a channel the scammer did not control, independent of the screen showing the balance.

What is not established is who operated the scheme, whether anyone was arrested or charged, and whether any of the money was recovered. Investigators' statement that victims in these cases rarely recover their funds is a general observation about such cases, not a finding about this one.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started when a stranger contacted them through WhatsApp. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app, gradually increasing the amounts while allowing small withdrawals to build trust. However, the scammer had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false investment gains on the screen. When Jerry attempted to withdraw a larger sum, he discovered the money was gone and called police.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Police confirmed the trading app itself was real, but the scammers manipulated what the couple saw on their screen. Investigators indicate that victims in these cases rarely recover their funds. The couple's children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help with their daily expenses as they work with Gwinnett County police on the matter.
